Notes

Versions 1 to 8 are deleted (you: "Delete this design ... Not just 3 lame ones that look like coffins"). Version 10 takes the shape language of your examples ("they looked menacing!"), never their designs: lances and prongs reaching past the bow, a hood over a narrow neck, low raked blades sweeping forward and down, fins raked aft, chevrons, the mass heavy aft, light in strips along booms and blades. Each blockout is a different arrangement of it, about 100 m long (the Concord Petrel is 88 m). Pick the ones worth taking further; each then gets its rooms, its tradition and its detail.

Version 12. Your picks: Hooded lance, Forked prow, Harpoon and Trident; Spearhead is withdrawn. Each pick is now one grown structure (you: "shapes must be made with purpose and flow into the grater structures"): one body lofted through sections of one layout, its prongs, lance, hood, blade and rail split from the body's own section and lofted on, light strips as faces of the skin, the drive a recess in the stern. Nothing is placed on it (Ship Design Bible, chapter 14).

Each pick has its own unwrap, its own painted colour map with its plating, chevrons and lit ports, and its AO baked (you: "ALL SHIPS MUST AVOID REPETTIVE TILE FOR MAIN COLOR MAP"); the chevron tile shows on it only faintly, as detail (chapter 15). The unpicked seven keep the tile and their version 10 build, as the record.

None is drawn from the species' body (Ship Design Bible, chapter 13).

Survey H4 is answered by your picks. Open the survey.
